classification.difficultyReason: Calculate shaded and remaining areas from composite diagrams, then simplify their ratio; sector areas require proportional reasoning.

inlines.text: Using the dimensions provided, find the ratio of the
for each of the following diagrams. (Hint: keep circle areas exact in terms of π where needed, then simplify the ratio).

spec.description: A 10 cm by 5 cm outer rectangle contains a shaded 4 cm by 2 cm rectangle toward the lower-left.
spec.mathematics: Outer area 50 cm²; shaded area 8 cm²; remaining area 42 cm².
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied dimensions are visible; calculated areas and ratios belong to answers.

answer.worked:
$\begin{align*}A_{\text{shaded}}&=4\times2=8\text{ cm}^2\\A_{\text{whole}}&=10\times5=50\text{ cm}^2\\A_{\text{unshaded}}&=50-8=42\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$
Divide both parts by $2$:
$\begin{align*}\text{shaded}:\text{unshaded}&=8:42\\\text{shaded}:\text{unshaded}&=4:21\end{align*}$

spec.description: A 20 cm by 15 cm rectangle contains two separate shaded triangles, pointing upward at lower-left and downward at upper-right. Their shared base and height annotation remains to the right.
spec.mathematics: Each triangle has base 10 cm and height 9 cm, giving total shaded area 90 cm² and remaining area 210 cm².
spec.answerVisibility: Dimensions and shared triangle annotation remain visible; calculated areas and ratios are answers.

spec.description: A smaller unshaded circle is offset upward inside a larger shaded circle. Separate centre markers identify the smaller circle's upper-right radius and the larger circle's downward radius.
spec.mathematics: The smaller radius is 4 cm and the larger radius is 8 cm. The centres are distinct; the shaded area is the difference of the two circle areas.
spec.answerVisibility: The two radii and centre markers remain visible; area calculations and ratios are answers.

answer.worked:
$\begin{align*}A_{\text{large circle}}&=\pi\times8^2=64\pi\text{ cm}^2\\A_{\text{unshaded}}&=\pi\times4^2=16\pi\text{ cm}^2\\A_{\text{shaded}}&=64\pi-16\pi=48\pi\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$
Divide both parts by $16\pi$:
$\begin{align*}\text{shaded}:\text{unshaded}&=48\pi:16\pi\\\text{shaded}:\text{unshaded}&=3:1\end{align*}$

spec.description: A circle has two white upper sectors labelled 30° and 50°. The remaining region, including the lower semicircle and the central upper sector, is shaded. All source radii and both angle arcs are retained.
spec.mathematics: Unshaded central angles total 80°; shaded central angles total 280°. Areas in the same circle are proportional to their central angles.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied 30° and 50° labels appear; totals and ratios belong to answers.

answer.worked:
Sector areas in the same circle are proportional to their central angles.
$\begin{align*}\theta_{\text{unshaded}}&=30^\circ+50^\circ=80^\circ\\\theta_{\text{shaded}}&=360^\circ-80^\circ=280^\circ\end{align*}$
Divide both parts by $40$:
$\begin{align*}\text{shaded}:\text{unshaded}&=280:80\\\text{shaded}:\text{unshaded}&=7:2\end{align*}$
